tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.

There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: SendUserFile
tools.description:
Send files to the user. Use this for any file the user would want to see — a generated diagram, a report, a screenshot, a built artifact — and you want it surfaced, not just mentioned. Send deliverables as they are produced, not batched at the end of the task: a complete draft or a meaningfully updated version of the thing the user asked for is worth sending mid-task, so they can follow progress and redirect early. Do NOT send routine working files — scratch files, debug output, partial fragments, or every incremental save of something you're still actively editing; each call renders a file card in the conversation, and a stream of cards for one file is noise. Re-send a file only when it has meaningfully changed since the last send. Paths can be absolute or relative to the current working directory.

Add a `caption` when a one-liner of context helps ("the failing case is row 42", "before vs after"). Skip it if the file speaks for itself.

Set `status` on every call. Use `proactive` when you're initiating — the user is away and you want this to reach their phone (build artifact ready, report generated). Use `normal` when replying to something the user just said.

Set `display` to choose how the file is presented. Use `'render'` when the user should see the content inline in the side panel right now — a chart, a rendered HTML page, a diagram, an image. Use `'attach'` when the file is something they'll save and open elsewhere — source code, a spreadsheet, a document for another app — and an inline preview would just be noise. Leave it unset to let the client decide by file type.

Files must already exist on the local filesystem — the tool sends files, it doesn't fetch URLs or render content. When unsure of a path, verify with ls first; absolute paths avoid ambiguity about the working directory.

Example: SendUserFile({ files: ["report.md"], caption: "Here's the report.", status: "normal" })

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

If the topic is serious — illness, disease, pandemics, death, grief, war, conflict, poverty, disaster, trauma, abuse, addiction, medical decisions, politically charged subjects, or anything where the reader might be personally affected — keep these BORING: describe what the code is doing in the dullest generic way, no jargon-as-drama, no evocative terms. """The spine planner: plans laid out the way an architect sketches them.

The genetic search partitions a rectangle and hopes the partition reads as a
house. This does the opposite: it starts from the parti most good Indian
houses share and fits the programme to it.

* A **hall spine** runs from the front door to the back. Every room opens off
  it, so no bedroom is reached through the living room, no toilet opens onto
  the dining table, and nobody walks through one room to reach another.
* Rooms sit in two **stacks**, one either side of the spine, so every room has
  a door on the spine and a window on an outside wall. Small rooms (puja,
  utility, powder room) share a row side by side rather than becoming slots.
* The **stair** is one rectangle beside the spine, identical on every floor.
* A bedroom and its **attached bath** are a suite: the bath behind the room,
  on the same outside wall.
* Rooms are **sized, not stretched**: a stack is as wide and as deep as its
  rooms want to be, capped at what a room of its kind usefully is. A big plot
  gets a bigger house (more and more generous rooms, set by the programme),
  with the rest of the plot left as garden rather than turned into a 70 m2
  dining room.

Everything is computed in a canonical frame (the road at the front, high v)
and turned to the real road at the end. Variants - which side the public rooms
take, where the stair sits, suite order, snug or generous stacks - give the
selector real choices.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import itertools
from dataclasses import dataclass, replace

from aip.domain.geometry import BoundingBox, Direction, Vec2, rectangle
from aip.domain.plan import Room, RoomType

T = RoomType
BEDS = {T.MASTER_BEDROOM, T.BEDROOM, T.GUEST_BEDROOM, T.CHILDREN_BEDROOM}
PUBLIC = [T.LIVING, T.DRAWING, T.FAMILY, T.DINING, T.KITCHEN, T.PANTRY, T.UTILITY, T.LAUNDRY]
SKIP = {T.STAIRCASE, T.CORRIDOR, T.LOBBY, T.SHAFT, T.FOYER, T.WARDROBE}
#: Rooms small enough to share a row with a neighbour.
SMALL = {T.PUJA, T.UTILITY, T.LAUNDRY, T.POWDER, T.TOILET, T.STORE, T.PANTRY, T.BATHROOM}
UNDER = {T.KITCHEN: 1.0, T.DINING: 1.0, T.PUJA: 1.5, T.LIVING: 0.4, T.DRAWING: 0.4}
WETS = {T.UTILITY, T.LAUNDRY, T.POWDER, T.TOILET, T.BATHROOM}
#: The smallest dimension a room can have and still be furnished.
MIN_DIM = {T.MASTER_BEDROOM: 3.4, T.BEDROOM: 3.0, T.GUEST_BEDROOM: 3.0, T.CHILDREN_BEDROOM: 3.0,
           T.LIVING: 4.2, T.DINING: 3.0, T.KITCHEN: 2.4, T.BATHROOM: 1.6, T.TOILET: 1.4, T.POWDER: 1.3,
           T.UTILITY: 1.4, T.PUJA: 1.4, T.STUDY: 2.6, T.FAMILY: 3.2, T.DRAWING: 3.4, T.GARAGE: 5.0,
           T.STORE: 1.4, T.BALCONY: 1.5, T.VERANDAH: 1.8, T.COURTYARD: 3.0, T.FOYER: 1.8, T.HOME_THEATRE: 3.6, T.GYM: 3.0, T.LIBRARY: 2.6, T.HOME_OFFICE: 2.6, T.SERVANT: 2.6}
#: The least a room can be and still be furnished, for floors with no room to spare.
MIN_AREA = {T.LIVING: 15.0, T.DINING: 8.5, T.KITCHEN: 6.5, T.MASTER_BEDROOM: 12.0, T.BEDROOM: 9.5,
            T.GUEST_BEDROOM: 9.5, T.CHILDREN_BEDROOM: 9.5, T.GARAGE: 14.0, T.COURTYARD: 9.0, T.BATHROOM: 3.2,
            T.TOILET: 2.2, T.UTILITY: 2.5, T.LAUNDRY: 3.0, T.PUJA: 2.0, T.STUDY: 7.0, T.FAMILY: 10.0}
#: How far a room may grow past its programme area; beyond it the plot is garden.
GROW = 1.1
SPINE = 1.3
FOYER = 1.9
STAIR_W, STAIR_L = 2.5, 4.6
BATH_DEPTH = 1.7


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Item:
    type: RoomType
    area: float
    req: object | None = None
    bath: Item | None = None


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Row:
    """One row of a stack: one room, a suite's bath, or small rooms side by side."""
    parts: list[Item]
    suite: bool = False
    depth: float = 0.0
    cap: float = 0.0
    grow: bool = True
    widths: list | None = None     # explicit widths, hall side first, for rooms side by side


@dataclass(slots=True)
class Variant:
    public_left: bool
    stair_at: float
    bath_behind: bool
    wide: float          # 0 snug .. 1 generous stacks
    transverse: bool = False   # spine parallel to the road (wide, shallow plots)
    single: bool = False       # narrow plots: one row of rooms beside a side hall
    ell: bool = False          # the living wing reaches past the bedrooms: an L-shaped house


def variants() -> list[Variant]:
    return [Variant(pl, sa, bb, w, tr) for tr, pl, sa, bb, w in
            itertools.product((False, True), (True, False), (0.3, 0.7), (True, False), (0.0, 1.0))
            if not (tr and pl)] + [Variant(pl, sa, True, 0.0, tr, True) for pl in (True, False) for sa in (0.0, 0.4) for tr in (False, True)]         + [Variant(pl, 0.0, True, 0.0, tr) for pl in (True, False) for tr in (False, True) if not (tr and pl)]


def _items(reqs: list) -> list[Item]:
    items = [Item(r.type, float(r.target_area), r) for r in reqs if r.type not in SKIP]
    beds = sorted([i for i in items if i.type in BEDS], key=lambda i: (i.type is not T.MASTER_BEDROOM, -i.area))
    baths = sorted([i for i in items if i.type in {T.BATHROOM, T.TOILET}], key=lambda i: -i.area)
    # With fewer baths than bedrooms, one stays common, off the hall, so the
    # bedrooms without their own still have a bathroom they can reach.
    attach = len(baths) - (1 if 0 < len(baths) < len(beds) else 0)
    for bed in beds[:attach]:
        bed.bath = baths.pop(0)
        items.remove(bed.bath)
        if bed.req is not None and hasattr(bed.req, "attached_bathroom"):
            bed.req.attached_bathroom = True
    return items


ORDER_PUB = [T.FOYER, T.DRAWING, T.LIVING, T.DINING, T.KITCHEN, T.PANTRY, T.UTILITY, T.LAUNDRY]

  the dining table, and nobody walks through one room to reach another.
* Rooms sit in two **stacks**, one either side of the spine, so every room has
  a door on the spine and a window on an outside wall. Small rooms (puja,
  utility, powder room) share a row side by side rather than becoming slots.

        wq = ql[1] - ql[0]

        # as a dog-leg of about 11 m2 needs: 3.8 m when narrow, less when wide.

        for li, (pub, priv, fronts) in enumerate(split):
            head = FOYER if li == 0 and not v.transverse and not v.single else 0.0
            # Upstairs, the side over the kitchen puts each bath in front of its
            # bedroom (toward the living room), not over the kitchen at the back.

            fitted = self._fit_level(pub, priv, fronts, pl[1] - pl[0], ql[1] - ql[0], D - ver, stair_len + head, vv)
            if fitted is None:

            prow, qrow, fronts = fitted
            fdepth = sum(max(1.5, min(1.8 if i.type is T.BALCONY else 3.0, i.area / (ql[1] - ql[0]))) for i in fronts)
            need_d = max(need_d, sum(r.depth for r in prow) + ver, sum(r.depth for r in qrow) + stair_len + fdepth + head + ver)
            cap_d = max(cap_d, sum(r.cap for r in prow), sum(r.cap for r in qrow) + stair_len + fdepth + head)

        if need_d > D + 1e-6:

            su0 = ql[1] - sw if v.public_left else ql[0]

            rooms: list[Room] = []

                    return

                                if r is not hall and r.metadata.get("_c") and abs(r.metadata["_c"][1] - min(bottoms)) < 0.01

    def _flip_suites(self, rs: list[Row], u0: float, u1: float, hi: float) -> None:
        """Upstairs, put each suite's bath at whichever end of its bedroom sits
        over less of the kitchen, dining and puja below."""
        def bad(b0: float, b1: float) -> float:
            return sum(w * max(0.0, min(u1, c[2]) - max(u0, c[0])) * max(0.0, min(b1, c[3]) - max(b0, c[1]))
                       for w, c in self.below)
        k, cursor = 0, hi
        while k < len(rs):
            pair = (k + 1 < len(rs) and rs[k].suite != rs[k + 1].suite
                    and any(p.type in BEDS for p in (rs[k + 1] if rs[k].suite else rs[k]).parts))
            if not pair:
                cursor -= rs[k].depth; k += 1
                continue
            first, second = rs[k], rs[k + 1]
            bath_first = first.suite
            bd = (first if bath_first else second).depth
            top = cursor - first.depth - second.depth
            now = bad(cursor - bd, cursor) if bath_first else bad(top, top + bd)
            alt = bad(top, top + bd) if bath_first else bad(cursor - bd, cursor)
            if alt < now - 0.3:
                rs[k], rs[k + 1] = second, first
            cursor = top; k += 2

    def _fit_level(self, pub, priv, fronts, wp, wq, D, stair_len, v):
        """Make a floor's programme fit its two stacks, the way a designer would:
        move a bedroom suite to the other side of the hall, then let go of the
        extras the programme added to fill a generous plot, then draw rooms a
        little smaller - never below what they need to be furnished."""
        pub, priv, fronts = list(pub), list(priv), list(fronts)
        optional = [T.COURTYARD, T.VERANDAH, T.HOME_THEATRE, T.GYM, T.LIBRARY, T.FAMILY, T.STUDY, T.TERRACE,
                    T.GARAGE, T.BALCONY, T.STORE, T.FOYER]   # an entrance hall last: the living room can receive
        def depth(items, w, extra=0.0, scale=1.0):
            saved = [(i, i.area) for i in items] + [(i.bath, i.bath.area) for i in items if i.bath]
            for i, a in saved:
                i.area = shrink(i, a, scale)
            rows = self._rows(items, w, v)
            for i, a in saved:
                i.area = a
            return sum(r.depth for r in rows) + extra
        def fdep():
            return sum(max(1.5, min(1.8 if i.type is T.BALCONY else 3.0, i.area / wq)) for i in fronts)
        def shrink(i, a, scale):
            # Draw a room smaller than the generous size the programme grew it
            # to, but never below 85 % of what the client asked for - or, on a
            # plot that cannot hold a hall otherwise, 72 %, and never so small
            # it cannot be furnished.
            asked = getattr(i.req, "asked_area", None) or a
            if scale >= 0.8:
                floor = asked * 0.85
            elif scale >= 0.7:
                floor = max(asked * 0.72, MIN_DIM.get(i.type, 1.4) ** 2 * 1.05)
            else:
                # Last resort on an over-full floor: the least each room can be furnished in.
                floor = MIN_AREA.get(i.type, MIN_DIM.get(i.type, 1.4) ** 2 * 1.05)
            return max(a * scale, min(a, floor))
        for scale in (1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5):
            for _ in range(12):
                dp, dq = depth(pub, wp, 0.0, scale), depth(priv, wq, stair_len + fdep() + (1.0 if stair_len and 0.0 < v.stair_at < 1.0 else 0.0), scale)
                if dp <= D + 1e-6 and dq <= D + 1e-6:
                    if scale < 1.0:
                        for i in pub + priv:
                            i.area = shrink(i, i.area, scale)
                            if i.bath:
                                i.bath.area = max(shrink(i.bath, i.bath.area, scale), 3.2)
                    return self._rows(pub, wp, v), self._rows(priv, wq, v), fronts

                src, dst, ws, wd = (priv, pub, wq, wp) if dq > dp else (pub, priv, wp, wq)
                if wp <= 0:
                    src, dst, ws, wd = priv, [], wq, 0.0
                # A bedroom, a study, a puja.
                movable = [i for i in src if i.type in BEDS
                           or i.type in {T.STUDY, T.FAMILY, T.STORE, T.PUJA, T.COURTYARD}]
                moved = False
                for it in (sorted(movable, key=lambda i: -(i.area + (i.bath.area if i.bath else 0))) if wd > 0 else []):
                    trial_src = [i for i in src if i is not it]
                    trial_dst = dst + [it]
                    a_src = depth(trial_src, ws, (stair_len + fdep()) if src is priv else 0.0, scale)
                    a_dst = depth(trial_dst, wd, (stair_len + fdep()) if dst is priv else 0.0, scale)
                    if max(a_src, a_dst) < max(dp, dq) - 0.05:
                        src.remove(it); dst.append(it)
                        moved = True

                if moved:

                # Let go of the extras, least needed first.
                for t in optional:

                    pool = [x for x in (fronts if t in {T.TERRACE, T.BALCONY} else (priv if dq > dp else pub))
                            if x.type is t and "Requested" not in (getattr(x.req, "notes", "") or "")]
                    if pool:
                        (fronts if t in {T.TERRACE, T.BALCONY} else (priv if dq > dp else pub)).remove(pool[-1])
                        moved = True
                        break
                if not moved:
                    break
        return None

        """Stop the hall at the last door it serves; the back room on one side

358	    def _flip_suites(self, rs: list[Row], u0: float, u1: float, hi: float) -> None:
359	        """Upstairs, put each suite's bath at whichever end of its bedroom sits
360	        over less of the kitchen, dining and puja below."""
361	        def bad(b0: float, b1: float) -> float:
362	            return sum(w * max(0.0, min(u1, c[2]) - max(u0, c[0])) * max(0.0, min(b1, c[3]) - max(b0, c[1]))
363	                       for w, c in self.below)
364	        k, cursor = 0, hi
365	        while k < len(rs):
366	            pair = (k + 1 < len(rs) and rs[k].suite != rs[k + 1].suite
367	                    and any(p.type in BEDS for p in (rs[k + 1] if rs[k].suite else rs[k]).parts))
368	            if not pair:
369	                cursor -= rs[k].depth; k += 1
370	                continue
371	            first, second = rs[k], rs[k + 1]
372	            bath_first = first.suite
373	            bd = (first if bath_first else second).depth
374	            top = cursor - first.depth - second.depth
375	            now = bad(cursor - bd, cursor) if bath_first else bad(top, top + bd)
376	            alt = bad(top, top + bd) if bath_first else bad(cursor - bd, cursor)
377	            if alt < now - 0.3:
378	                rs[k], rs[k + 1] = second, first
379	            cursor = top; k += 2

381	    def _fit_level(self, pub, priv, fronts, wp, wq, D, stair_len, v):
382	        """Make a floor's programme fit its two stacks, the way a designer would:
383	        move a bedroom suite to the other side of the hall, then let go of the
384	        extras the programme added to fill a generous plot, then draw rooms a
385	        little smaller - never below what they need to be furnished."""
386	        pub, priv, fronts = list(pub), list(priv), list(fronts)
387	        optional = [T.COURTYARD, T.VERANDAH, T.HOME_THEATRE, T.GYM, T.LIBRARY, T.FAMILY, T.STUDY, T.TERRACE,
388	                    T.GARAGE, T.BALCONY, T.STORE, T.FOYER]   # an entrance hall last: the living room can receive
389	        def depth(items, w, extra=0.0, scale=1.0):
390	            saved = [(i, i.area) for i in items] + [(i.bath, i.bath.area) for i in items if i.bath]
391	            for i, a in saved:
392	                i.area = shrink(i, a, scale)
393	            rows = self._rows(items, w, v)
394	            for i, a in saved:
395	                i.area = a
396	            return sum(r.depth for r in rows) + extra
397	        def fdep():
398	            return sum(max(1.5, min(1.8 if i.type is T.BALCONY else 3.0, i.area / wq)) for i in fronts)
399	        def shrink(i, a, scale):
400	            # Draw a room smaller than the generous size the programme grew it
401	            # to, but never below 85 % of what the client asked for - or, on a
402	            # plot that cannot hold a hall otherwise, 72 %, and never so small
403	            # it cannot be furnished.
404	            asked = getattr(i.req, "asked_area", None) or a
405	            if scale >= 0.8:
406	                floor = asked * 0.85
407	            elif scale >= 0.7:
408	                floor = max(asked * 0.72, MIN_DIM.get(i.type, 1.4) ** 2 * 1.05)
409	            else:
410	                # Last resort on an over-full floor: the least each room can be furnished in.
411	                floor = MIN_AREA.get(i.type, MIN_DIM.get(i.type, 1.4) ** 2 * 1.05)
412	            return max(a * scale, min(a, floor))
413	        for scale in (1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5):
414	            for _ in range(12):
415	                dp, dq = depth(pub, wp, 0.0, scale), depth(priv, wq, stair_len + fdep() + (1.0 if stair_len and 0.0 < v.stair_at < 1.0 else 0.0), scale)
416	                if dp <= D + 1e-6 and dq <= D + 1e-6:
417	                    if scale < 1.0:
418	                        for i in pub + priv:
419	                            i.area = shrink(i, i.area, scale)
420	                            if i.bath:
421	                                i.bath.area = max(shrink(i.bath, i.bath.area, scale), 3.2)
422	                    return self._rows(pub, wp, v), self._rows(priv, wq, v), fronts
423	                # Move a suite or room across the hall to the emptier side.
424	                src, dst, ws, wd = (priv, pub, wq, wp) if dq > dp else (pub, priv, wp, wq)
425	                if wp <= 0:
426	                    src, dst, ws, wd = priv, [], wq, 0.0
427	                # A bedroom, a study, a puja.
428	                movable = [i for i in src if i.type in BEDS
429	                           or i.type in {T.STUDY, T.FAMILY, T.STORE, T.PUJA, T.COURTYARD}]
430	                moved = False
431	                for it in (sorted(movable, key=lambda i: -(i.area + (i.bath.area if i.bath else 0))) if wd > 0 else []):
432	                    trial_src = [i for i in src if i is not it]
433	                    trial_dst = dst + [it]
434	                    a_src = depth(trial_src, ws, (stair_len + fdep()) if src is priv else 0.0, scale)
435	                    a_dst = depth(trial_dst, wd, (stair_len + fdep()) if dst is priv else 0.0, scale)
436	                    if max(a_src, a_dst) < max(dp, dq) - 0.05:
437	                        src.remove(it); dst.append(it)
438	                        moved = True
439	                        break
440	                if moved:
441	                    continue
442	                # Let go of the extras, least needed first.
443	                for t in optional:
444	                    # Never what the client asked for - only what the programme added.
445	                    pool = [x for x in (fronts if t in {T.TERRACE, T.BALCONY} else (priv if dq > dp else pub))
446	                            if x.type is t and "Requested" not in (getattr(x.req, "notes", "") or "")]
447	                    if pool:
448	                        (fronts if t in {T.TERRACE, T.BALCONY} else (priv if dq > dp else pub)).remove(pool[-1])
449	                        moved = True
450	                        break
451	                if not moved:
452	                    break
453	        return None

455	    def _trim_hall(self, rooms: list[Room], li: int, spine, v0: float) -> None:
456	        """Stop the hall at the last door it serves; the back room on one side
457	        takes the end of the spine instead of leaving a dead-end passage."""
458	        s0, s1 = spine
459	        canon = {id(r): r.metadata.get("_c") for r in rooms}
460	        hall = next((r for r in rooms if r.type is T.CORRIDOR), None)
461	        if hall is None:
462	            return
463	        backs = []

outer: BoundingBox | None = None, side: int = 0) -> None:
        self.env = envelope
        r = (road.cardinal if road is not None else Direction.N).value
        # A road on a diagonal (south-west) fronts one of its two sides; the
        # caller tries each (`side` 0 or 1).
        self.road = r if r in {"N", "S", "E", "W"} else (r[side] if len(r) == 2 and r[side] in "NSEW" else "N")
        across_x = self.road in {"N", "S"}
        self.W = envelope.width if across_x else envelope.height
        self.D = envelope.height if across_x else envelope.width
        self.stair_on = stair_on
        # How far the buildable plot reaches past the envelope on each side of
        # the frontage (canonical low and high u): room for an L's wing.
        o = outer or envelope
        e = envelope
        gap = {"N": (e.min_x - o.min_x, o.max_x - e.max_x), "S": (o.max_x - e.max_x, e.min_x - o.min_x),
               "E": (o.max_y - e.max_y, e.min_y - o.min_y), "W": (e.min_y - o.min_y, o.max_y - e.max_y)}[self.road]
        self.slack = (max(0.0, gap[0]), max(0.0, gap[1]))

    def _poly(self, u0: float, v0: float, u1: float, v1: float):
        if getattr(self, "tr", False):
            u0, v0, u1, v1 = v0, u0, v1, u1
        e, W, D = self.env, self.W, self.D
        if self.road == "N":
            x0, y0, x1, y1 = e.min_x + u0, e.min_y + v0, e.min_x + u1, e.min_y + v1
        elif self.road == "S":
            x0, y0, x1, y1 = e.min_x + (W - u1), e.min_y + (D - v1), e.min_x + (W - u0), e.min_y + (D - v0)
        elif self.road == "E":
            x0, y0, x1, y1 = e.min_x + v0, e.min_y + (W - u1), e.min_x + v1, e.min_y + (W - u0)
        else:
            x0, y0, x1, y1 = e.min_x + (D - v1), e.min_y + u0, e.min_x + (D - v0), e.min_y + u1
        return rectangle(Vec2(x0, y0), x1 - x0, y1 - y0)

    def _rows(self, items: list[Item], width: float, v: Variant) -> list[Row]:
        rows: list[Row] = []
        smalls: list[Item] = []

        def flush():
            while smalls:
                take, used = [], 0.0
                while smalls and len(take) < 3 and used + max(MIN_DIM.get(smalls[0].type, 1.4), 1.6) <= width + 1e-6:
                    if take and ((smalls[0].type is T.PUJA) != (take[0].type is T.PUJA)):
                        break
                    it = smalls.pop(0)
                    take.append(it)
                    used += max(MIN_DIM.get(it.type, 1.4), 1.6)
                if not take:
                    take = [smalls.pop(0)]
                area = sum(i.area for i in take)
                # Alone, a small room runs the stack's width at its minimum depth.
                d = (max(1.2, 5.5 / width) if take[0].type is T.PUJA else max(MIN_DIM.get(take[0].type, 1.4), 1.5))                     if len(take) == 1 else max(area / width, 1.6)
                rows.append(Row(take, depth=d, cap=max(d, 2.4), grow=False))

        pending = list(items)
        while pending:
            it = pending.pop(0)
            if it.type in SMALL and it.bath is None:
                smalls.append(it)
                continue
            flush()
            mn = MIN_DIM.get(it.type, 2.4)
            # A wide stack takes two rooms side by side: a bedroom with its bath
            # beyond it, or the dining room with the kitchen beyond it.
            if it.bath is not None and width >= mn + 1.8:
                bw = min(2.4, max(1.6, width - mn - 0.0)) if width < mn + 2.4 else 2.0
                d = max(it.area / (width - bw), mn, it.bath.area / bw, 2.0)
                rows.append(Row([it, it.bath], depth=d, cap=d, grow=False, widths=[width - bw, bw]))
                continue
            nxt = pending[0] if pending else None
            if it.type is T.DINING and nxt is not None and nxt.type is T.KITCHEN and width >= 5.4:
                pending.pop(0)
                wk = max(2.4, width * nxt.area / (nxt.area + it.area))
                d = max((it.area + nxt.area) / width, 3.0)
                rows.append(Row([it, nxt], depth=d, cap=d * 1.15, widths=[width - wk, wk]))
                continue
            d = max(it.area / width, MIN_DIM.get(it.type, 2.4))
            fixed = it.type in {T.VERANDAH, T.COURTYARD, T.GARAGE, T.FOYER, T.BALCONY}
            asked = getattr(it.req, "asked_area", None) or it.area
            main = Row([it], depth=d, cap=d if fixed else max(d, min(it.area * GROW, asked * 1.45) / width), grow=not fixed)
            if it.bath is not None:
                bath = Row([it.bath], suite=True, depth=BATH_DEPTH, cap=BATH_DEPTH, grow=False)
                rows.extend([main, bath] if v.bath_behind else [bath, main])
            else:
                rows.append(main)
        flush()
        # A puja never shares a wall with a toilet: move it away from wet rows.
        wet = lambda r: any(x.type in WETS for x in r.parts) or r.suite  # noqa: E731
        for k, r in enumerate(rows):
            if any(x.type is T.PUJA for x in r.parts):
                near = [rows[j] for j in (k - 1, k + 1) if 0 <= j < len(rows)]
                if any(wet(n) for n in near):
                    rows.pop(k)
                    spot = next((j for j in range(len(rows) + 1)
                                 if not any(wet(rows[x]) for x in (j - 1, j) if 0 <= x < len(rows))), None)
                    if spot is None:
                        # Nowhere clear of the wet rooms: a store between them.
                        rows.insert(0, r)
                        rows.insert(1, Row([Item(T.STORE, width * 1.3)], depth=1.3, cap=1.3, grow=False))
                    else:
                        rows.insert(spot, r)
                break
        return rows

    def plan(self, levels: list[list], v: Variant) -> list[list[Room]] | None:
        # Transverse: the same parti turned so the spine runs along the road.
        self.tr = v.transverse
        W, D = (self.D, self.W) if v.transverse else (self.W, self.D)
        self.outer = {}
        levels = [list(l) for l in levels]
        self.verandah = None
        self.garden = {}
        # Courtyards, verandahs and car porches are ground-floor rooms.
        for l in levels[1:]:
            for r in [r for r in l if r.type in {T.COURTYARD, T.VERANDAH, T.GARAGE}]:
                l.remove(r); levels[0].append(r)
        # A bedroom floor needs its bathrooms on it: pull a spare one from a floor that has more.
        def count(l, ts): return sum(1 for r in l if r.type in ts)
        for li, l in enumerate(levels):
            while count(l, BEDS) > count(l, {T.BATHROOM, T.TOILET}):
                donor = next((d for d in levels if d is not l and count(d, {T.BATHROOM, T.TOILET}) > max(count(d, BEDS), 1)), None)
                if donor is None:
                    break
                b = next(r for r in donor if r.type in {T.BATHROOM, T.TOILET})
                donor.remove(b); l.append(b)
        split = []
        for li, items in enumerate(_items(r) for r in levels):
            terr = [i for i in items if i.type is T.TERRACE]
            if len(terr) > 1:
                items = [i for i in items if i.type is not T.TERRACE] + [Item(T.TERRACE, min(sum(i.area for i in terr), 20.0), terr[0].req)]
            out = [i for i in items if i.type.is_outdoor or i.type is T.GARAGE]
            rest = [i for i in items if i not in out]
            pub = sorted([i for i in rest if i.type in PUBLIC], key=lambda i: ORDER_PUB.index(i.type))
            priv = sorted([i for i in rest if i not in pub], key=lambda i: RANK.get(i.type, 3))
            if li == 0 and v.transverse:
                # The spine no longer reaches the road: the foyer heads the public stack.
                pub.insert(0, Item(T.FOYER, 6.5))
            if li > 0 and not pub:
                # Bedrooms either side of the hall, balanced by depth (the
                # stair already takes some of the private side).
                pub, priv2, dp, dq = [], [], 0.0, STAIR_L if self.stair_on else 0.0
                for it in sorted(priv, key=lambda i: -(i.area + (i.bath.area if i.bath else 0))):
                    d = it.area / 4 + (BATH_DEPTH if it.bath else 0)
                    if dp <= dq:
                        pub.append(it); dp += d
                    else:
                        priv2.append(it); dq += d
                pub.sort(key=lambda i: RANK.get(i.type, 3)); priv = sorted(priv2, key=lambda i: RANK.get(i.type, 3))
            # Outdoor rooms: a sit-out heads the public stack, a car porch the
            # private one, a courtyard opens in the private stack; upstairs,
            # balconies and terraces take the front of the private stack.
            fronts = []
            for it in out:
                if li == 0 and it.type is T.VERANDAH:
                    if v.transverse:
                        pub.insert(1 if pub and pub[0].type is T.FOYER else 0, Item(T.VERANDAH, min(it.area, 9.0), it.req))
                    else:
                        self.verandah = Item(T.VERANDAH, it.area, it.req)   # a band across the front
                elif li == 0 and it.type is T.GARAGE:
                    # A car porch is on the road: the head of the private stack,
                    # or with the spine along the road, an end of the front stack.
                    if v.transverse:
                        # The road front then holds the porch and the living room; the
                        # dining room and kitchen, kept together, take the back stack.
                        pub.insert(1 if pub and pub[0].type is T.FOYER else 0, Item(T.GARAGE, it.area, it.req))
                        back = [x for x in pub if x.type in {T.DINING, T.KITCHEN, T.PANTRY, T.UTILITY, T.LAUNDRY}]
                        pub[:] = [x for x in pub if x not in back]
                        priv[:0] = back
                    else:
                        priv.insert(0, Item(T.GARAGE, it.area, it.req))
                elif li == 0 and it.type is T.COURTYARD:
                    priv.insert(min(2, len(priv)), Item(T.COURTYARD, min(it.area, 16.0), it.req))
                elif li > 0 and it.type in {T.BALCONY, T.TERRACE}:
                    fronts.append(Item(it.type, min(it.area, 8.0 if it.type is T.BALCONY else 14.0), it.req))
            # A balcony that opens off a named room goes beside that room, in its
            # stack, behind its suite - at the back wall, so it is open to the sky.
            for it in list(fronts):
                note = (getattr(it.req, "notes", "") or "").lower()
                if "opens off the" not in note:
                    continue
                host_name = note.split("opens off the", 1)[1].strip(" .")
                host_type = next((t for t in BEDS | {T.LIVING, T.FAMILY, T.STUDY, T.DINING, T.KITCHEN}
                                  if t.value.replace("_", " ") == host_name), None)
                for stack in (pub, priv):
                    host = next((x for x in stack if x.type is host_type), None)
                    if host is not None:
                        fronts.remove(it)
                        stack.insert(stack.index(host) + 1, Item(T.BALCONY, min(it.area, 7.0), it.req))
                        break
            split.append((pub, priv, fronts))

        def want(items, lo, hi):
            if not items:
                return lo
            need = max(MIN_DIM.get(i.type, 2.4) for i in items)
            return min(hi, max(lo, need + 0.2, (max(i.area for i in items) * 1.15) ** 0.5))
        hall_w = SPINE
        if v.single:
            # A narrow plot: every room in one row beside a side hall.
            split = [([], ([Item(T.FOYER, 4.5)] if li == 0 else [])
                      + [i for i in sorted(p, key=lambda i: ORDER_PUB.index(i.type) if i.type in ORDER_PUB else 0)] + q, f)
                     for li, (p, q, f) in enumerate(split)]
            hall_w = 1.2
            pw, qw = 0.0, min(W - hall_w, 6.5)
            if qw < 3.0:
                self.why = 1
                return None
        else:
            pw = max(want(p, 3.6, 4.6 + 1.6 * v.wide) for p, _, _ in split)
            qw = max(want(q, 3.2, min(3.6 if self.stair_on else 4.6, 4.2 + 1.4 * v.wide)) for _, q, _ in split)
        if self.stair_on:
            qw = max(qw, STAIR_W)
        if not v.single and pw + SPINE + qw > W:
            # A tight plot: the hall narrows to a passage (1.1 m) before the rooms do.
            hall_w = 1.1
            free = W - hall_w
            if free < 2 * 2.8:
                self.why = 2
                return None
            k = free / (pw + qw)
            pw, qw = pw * k, qw * k
        SP = hall_w
        self.spine = None
        Wh = pw + SP + qw
        u_off = (W - Wh) / 2 if not v.transverse else W - Wh   # transverse: the house against the road
        # An L: the public rooms at the front reach out past the bedroom wing,
        # leaving a garden court in the angle.
        self.ext = 0.0
        if v.ell and not v.transverse and not v.single:
            room = (W - Wh) + (self.slack[0] if v.public_left else self.slack[1])
            self.ext = min(4.5, room)
            if self.ext < 2.4:
                self.why = 9
                return None
            u_off = W - Wh if v.public_left else 0.0
        self.house = (u_off, u_off + Wh)
        if v.public_left:
            pl, spine, ql = (u_off, u_off + pw), (u_off + pw, u_off + pw + SP), (u_off + pw + SP, u_off + Wh)
        else:
            ql, spine, pl = (u_off, u_off + qw), (u_off + qw, u_off + qw + SP), (u_off + qw + SP, u_off + Wh)

        # A dog-leg of about 11 m2: deeper when the stack is narrow, shallower when wide.
        wq = ql[1] - ql[0]
        # The stair spans its stack (so it always opens onto the hall), as deep
        # as a dog-leg of about 11 m2 needs: 3.8 m when narrow, less when wide.
        sw = wq
        stair_len = 3.81 if self.stair_on else 0.0     # a dog-leg's run, whatever the stack width
        plans, need_d, cap_d = [], 0.0, 0.0
        for li, (pub, priv, fronts) in enumerate(split):
            head = FOYER if li == 0 and not v.transverse and not v.single else 0.0
            # Upstairs, the side over the kitchen puts each bath in front of its
            # bedroom (toward the living room), not over the kitchen at the back.
            vv = v if li == 0 else replace(v, bath_behind=False)
            ver = 1.8 if li == 0 and self.verandah is not None else 0.0
            fitted = self._fit_level(pub, priv, fronts, pl[1] - pl[0], ql[1] - ql[0], D - ver, stair_len + head, vv)
            if fitted is None:
                self.why = 3
                return None
            prow, qrow, fronts = fitted
            fdepth = sum(max(1.5, min(1.8 if i.type is T.BALCONY else 3.0, i.area / (ql[1] - ql[0]))) for i in fronts)
            need_d = max(need_d, sum(r.depth for r in prow) + ver, sum(r.depth for r in qrow) + stair_len + fdepth + head + ver)
            cap_d = max(cap_d, sum(r.cap for r in prow), sum(r.cap for r in qrow) + stair_len + fdepth + head)
            plans.append((prow, qrow, fronts))
        if need_d > D + 1e-6:
            self.why = 4
            return None
        Dh = min(D, max(need_d, cap_d))
        v0 = D - Dh
        self.spine = spine
        stair = None
        if self.stair_on:
            # The stair takes the stack's full width (a roomier landing) unless
            # the stack is wide enough to leave a useful room beside it.
            # The stair on the outer side; any strip between it and the hall is its landing lobby.
            su0 = ql[1] - sw if v.public_left else ql[0]
            free = Dh - STAIR_L
            head0 = (FOYER if not v.transverse and not v.single else 0.0) + (1.8 if self.verandah is not None else 0.0)
            free = Dh - stair_len - head0
            sv0 = v0 + free * v.stair_at
            # Never leave a sliver beside the stair that no room can use.
            if (D - head0) - (sv0 + stair_len) < 2.4:
                sv0 = D - head0 - stair_len
            if sv0 - v0 < 2.4:
                sv0 = v0
            stair = (su0, sv0, su0 + sw, sv0 + stair_len)

        out_levels = []
        for li, (prow, qrow, fronts) in enumerate(plans):
            rooms: list[Room] = []

            def add(t, a0, b0, a1, b1, req=None, name=None, _rooms=rooms, _li=li):
                if a1 - a0 < 0.9 or b1 - b0 < 0.9:
                    return
                area = round((a1 - a0) * (b1 - b0), 2)
                _rooms.append(Room(name=name or t.label, type=t, polygon=self._poly(a0, b0, a1, b1), level=_li,
                                   ceiling_height=3.0,
                                   metadata={"_c": (a0, b0, a1, b1), "notes": getattr(req, "notes", "") or "",
                                             "target_area": getattr(req, "target_area", None) or area,
                                             "brief_area": getattr(req, "asked_area", None) or getattr(req, "target_area", None) or area,
                                             "planner": "spine"}))
            s0, s1 = spine
            Dl = D
            if li == 0 and self.verandah is not None:
                # A covered verandah across the whole front, the house behind it.
                Dl = D - 1.8
                add(T.VERANDAH, self.house[0], Dl, self.house[1], D, self.verandah.req, name="Verandah")
            foyer_cut = 0.0
            if li == 0 and not v.transverse and not v.single:
                # The entrance hall: across the head of the hall and the front of
                # the private stack, so it opens straight onto the living room.
                fu0, fu1 = min(s0, ql[0]), max(s1, ql[1])
                add(T.FOYER, fu0, Dl - FOYER, fu1, Dl, name="Foyer")
                foyer_cut = FOYER
                add(T.CORRIDOR, s0, v0, s1, Dl - FOYER, name="Corridor")
            else:
                add(T.CORRIDOR, s0, v0, s1, Dl, name="Corridor")
            if stair:
                add(T.STAIRCASE, *stair, name="Staircase")
            self.level = li
            self.v0 = v0
            self.rooms_ref = rooms
            self.reach = self.ext if li == 0 else 0.0   # upstairs stays a simple block
            self.reach_low = v.public_left
            if not self._fill(add, pl, prow, v0, Dl, None, []):
                self.why = 5
                return None
            self.reach = 0.0
            if not self._fill(add, ql, qrow, v0, Dl - foyer_cut, stair, fronts):
                self.why = 6
                return None
            # The hall stops at the last door it serves; behind it is garden.
            # Decided on the ground floor and kept above, so floors stack.
            hall = next((r for r in rooms if r.type is T.CORRIDOR), None)
            if hall is not None:
                if li == 0:
                    sides = []
                    for lo_u, hi_u in (pl, ql):
                        bottoms = [r.metadata["_c"][1] for r in rooms
                                   if r is not hall and r.metadata.get("_c") and r.metadata["_c"][0] >= lo_u - 0.01
                                   and r.metadata["_c"][2] <= hi_u + 0.01]
                        tops = [r.metadata["_c"][3] for r in rooms
                                if r is not hall and r.metadata.get("_c") and abs(r.metadata["_c"][1] - min(bottoms)) < 0.01
                                and r.metadata["_c"][0] >= lo_u - 0.01 and r.metadata["_c"][2] <= hi_u + 0.01] if bottoms else []
                        if tops:
                            sides.append(min(bottoms) + min(1.2, (min(tops) - min(bottoms)) * 0.5))
                    self.hall_from = max(v0, min(sides)) if sides else v0
                hc = hall.metadata["_c"]
                start = max(hc[1], getattr(self, "hall_from", v0))
                if start > hc[1] + 0.05 and hc[3] - start > 1.0:
                    nc = (hc[0], start, hc[2], hc[3])
                    hall.polygon = self._poly(*nc); hall.metadata["_c"] = nc
            if li == 0:
                # What a bath upstairs must not sit over: a kitchen, a dining table, a shrine.
                self.below = [(UNDER.get(r.type, 0.0), r.metadata["_c"]) for r in rooms
                              if r.type in UNDER and r.metadata.get("_c")]
            out_levels.append(rooms)
        self.below = []
        return out_levels

    def _flip_suites(self, rs: list[Row], u0: float, u1: float, hi: float) -> None:
        """Upstairs, put each suite's bath at whichever end of its bedroom sits
        over less of the kitchen, dining and puja below."""
        def bad(b0: float, b1: float) -> float:
            return sum(w * max(0.0, min(u1, c[2]) - max(u0, c[0])) * max(0.0, min(b1, c[3]) - max(b0, c[1]))
                       for w, c in self.below)
        k, cursor = 0, hi
        while k < len(rs):
            pair = (k + 1 < len(rs) and rs[k].suite != rs[k + 1].suite
                    and any(p.type in BEDS for p in (rs[k + 1] if rs[k].suite else rs[k]).parts))
            if not pair:
                cursor -= rs[k].depth; k += 1
                continue
            first, second = rs[k], rs[k + 1]
            bath_first = first.suite
            bd = (first if bath_first else second).depth
            top = cursor - first.depth - second.depth
            now = bad(cursor - bd, cursor) if bath_first else bad(top, top + bd)
            alt = bad(top, top + bd) if bath_first else bad(cursor - bd, cursor)
            if alt < now - 0.3:
                rs[k], rs[k + 1] = second, first
            cursor = top; k += 2

    def _fit_level(self, pub, priv, fronts, wp, wq, D, stair_len, v):
        """Make a floor's programme fit its two stacks, the way a designer would:
        move a bedroom suite to the other side of the hall, then let go of the
        extras the programme added to fill a generous plot, then draw rooms a
        little smaller - never below what they need to be furnished."""
        pub, priv, fronts = list(pub), list(priv), list(fronts)
        optional = [T.COURTYARD, T.VERANDAH, T.HOME_THEATRE, T.GYM, T.LIBRARY, T.FAMILY, T.STUDY, T.TERRACE,
                    T.GARAGE, T.BALCONY, T.STORE, T.FOYER]   # an entrance hall last: the living room can receive
        def depth(items, w, extra=0.0, scale=1.0):
            saved = [(i, i.area) for i in items] + [(i.bath, i.bath.area) for i in items if i.bath]
            for i, a in saved:
                i.area = shrink(i, a, scale)
            rows = self._rows(items, w, v)
            for i, a in saved:
                i.area = a
            return sum(r.depth for r in rows) + extra
        def fdep():
            return sum(max(1.5, min(1.8 if i.type is T.BALCONY else 3.0, i.area / wq)) for i in fronts)
        def shrink(i, a, scale):
            # Draw a room smaller than the generous size the programme grew it
            # to, but never below 85 % of what the client asked for - or, on a
            # plot that cannot hold a hall otherwise, 72 %, and never so small
            # it cannot be furnished.
            asked = getattr(i.req, "asked_area", None) or a
            if scale >= 0.8:
                floor = asked * 0.85
            elif scale >= 0.7:
                floor = max(asked * 0.72, MIN_DIM.get(i.type, 1.4) ** 2 * 1.05)
            else:
                # Last resort on an over-full floor: the least each room can be furnished in.
                floor = MIN_AREA.get(i.type, MIN_DIM.get(i.type, 1.4) ** 2 * 1.05)
            return max(a * scale, min(a, floor))
        for scale in (1.0, 0.9, 0.8, 0.7, 0.6, 0.5):
            for _ in range(12):
                dp, dq = depth(pub, wp, 0.0, scale), depth(priv, wq, stair_len + fdep() + (1.0 if stair_len and 0.0 < v.stair_at < 1.0 else 0.0), scale)
                if dp <= D + 1e-6 and dq <= D + 1e-6:
                    if scale < 1.0:
                        for i in pub + priv:
                            i.area = shrink(i, i.area, scale)
                            if i.bath:
                                i.bath.area = max(shrink(i.bath, i.bath.area, scale), 3.2)
                    return self._rows(pub, wp, v), self._rows(priv, wq, v), fronts
                # Move a suite or room across the hall to the emptier side.
                src, dst, ws, wd = (priv, pub, wq, wp) if dq > dp else (pub, priv, wp, wq)
                if wp <= 0:
                    src, dst, ws, wd = priv, [], wq, 0.0
                # A bedroom, a study, a puja.
                movable = [i for i in src if i.type in BEDS
                           or i.type in {T.STUDY, T.FAMILY, T.STORE, T.PUJA, T.COURTYARD}]
                moved = False
                for it in (sorted(movable, key=lambda i: -(i.area + (i.bath.area if i.bath else 0))) if wd > 0 else []):
                    trial_src = [i for i in src if i is not it]
                    trial_dst = dst + [it]
                    a_src = depth(trial_src, ws, (stair_len + fdep()) if src is priv else 0.0, scale)
                    a_dst = depth(trial_dst, wd, (stair_len + fdep()) if dst is priv else 0.0, scale)
                    if max(a_src, a_dst) < max(dp, dq) - 0.05:
                        src.remove(it); dst.append(it)
                        moved = True
                        break
                if moved:
                    continue
                # Let go of the extras, least needed first.
                for t in optional:
                    # Never what the client asked for - only what the programme added.
                    pool = [x for x in (fronts if t in {T.TERRACE, T.BALCONY} else (priv if dq > dp else pub))
                            if x.type is t and "Requested" not in (getattr(x.req, "notes", "") or "")]
                    if pool:
                        (fronts if t in {T.TERRACE, T.BALCONY} else (priv if dq > dp else pub)).remove(pool[-1])
                        moved = True
                        break
                if not moved:
                    break
        return None

    def _trim_hall(self, rooms: list[Room], li: int, spine, v0: float) -> None:
        """Stop the hall at the last door it serves; the back room on one side
        takes the end of the spine instead of leaving a dead-end passage."""
        s0, s1 = spine
        canon = {id(r): r.metadata.get("_c") for r in rooms}
        hall = next((r for r in rooms if r.type is T.CORRIDOR), None)
        if hall is None:
            return
        backs = []
        for side in ((None, s0), (s1, None)):
            cands = [r for r in rooms if r is not hall and canon[id(r)] and abs(canon[id(r)][1] - v0) < 0.01
                     and ((side[1] is not None and abs(canon[id(r)][2] - s0) < 0.01) or (side[0] is not None and abs(canon[id(r)][0] - s1) < 0.01))]
            if cands:
                backs.append(cands[0])
        if len(backs) != 2:
            return
        a, b = sorted(backs, key=lambda r: canon[id(r)][3] - canon[id(r)][1])
        da, db = canon[id(a)][3] - v0, canon[id(b)][3] - v0
        if db - da < 1.0 or a.type in {T.STAIRCASE, T.TERRACE} or a.type.is_wet:
            return
        hc = canon[id(hall)]
        # The shallower back room widens across the spine; the hall starts above it.
        ac = canon[id(a)]
        na = (min(ac[0], s0), ac[1], max(ac[2], s1), ac[3])
        nh = (hc[0], v0 + da, hc[2], hc[3])
        a.polygon = self._poly(*na); a.metadata["_c"] = na
        hall.polygon = self._poly(*nh); hall.metadata["_c"] = nh

    def _fill(self, add, side, rows: list[Row], v0: float, D: float, stair, fronts: list[Item]) -> bool:
        u0, u1 = side
        width = u1 - u0
        g = self.garden.get((round(u0, 2), round(u1, 2))) if self.level > 0 else None
        if g:
            v0 = g
        spans = [(v0, D)]
        if stair and stair[0] < u1 - 0.01 and stair[2] > u0 + 0.01:
            sv0, sv1 = stair[1], stair[3]
            if width - (stair[2] - stair[0]) >= 1.4:
                inner = (stair[2], u1) if stair[0] <= u0 + 0.01 else (u0, stair[0])
                add(T.STORE, inner[0], sv0, inner[1], sv1, name="Store")
            spans = [(sv1, D), (v0, sv0)]
        top = D
        front_floor = max(lo for lo, hi in spans if hi >= D - 1e-6)   # the stair, if it sits at the front
        for it in fronts:
            d = max(1.5, min(1.8 if it.type is T.BALCONY else 3.0, it.area / width))
            if top - d < front_floor - 1e-6:
                continue            # no room in front of the stair; the floor's leftover becomes terrace
            add(it.type, u0, top - d, u1, top, it.req)
            top -= d
        bins = [[lo, min(hi, top)] for lo, hi in spans if min(hi, top) - lo > 0.05]
        reach = getattr(self, "reach", 0.0)
        if reach and rows and len(rows[0].parts) == 1 and rows[0].parts[0].type in (T.LIVING, T.DRAWING, T.VERANDAH):
            it = rows[0].parts[0]
            asked = getattr(it.req, "asked_area", None) or it.area
            rows[0].depth = max(MIN_DIM.get(it.type, 3.6), it.area / (width + reach))
            rows[0].cap = max(rows[0].depth, asked * 1.4 / (width + reach))
        groups, k = [], 0
        while k < len(rows):
            g = [rows[k]]
            if k + 1 < len(rows) and rows[k].suite != rows[k + 1].suite and (rows[k].suite or rows[k + 1].suite):
                g.append(rows[k + 1])
            groups.append(g)
            k += len(g)
        placed: list[list[Row]] = [[] for _ in bins]
        bi, left = 0, (bins[0][1] - bins[0][0]) if bins else 0.0
        for g in groups:
            gd = sum(r.depth for r in g)
            while bi < len(bins) and gd > left + 1e-6:
                bi += 1
                left = (bins[bi][1] - bins[bi][0]) if bi < len(bins) else 0.0
            if bi >= len(bins):
                return False
            placed[bi].extend(g)
            left -= gd
        for (lo, hi), rs in zip(bins, placed, strict=True):
            spare = (hi - lo) - sum(r.depth for r in rs)
            for _ in range(4):
                room_for = [r for r in rs if r.grow and r.cap - r.depth > 1e-3]
                if spare <= 1e-3 or not room_for:
                    break
                share = spare / len(room_for)
                for r in room_for:
                    d = min(share, r.cap - r.depth)
                    r.depth += d
                    spare -= d
            # What is left after every room reached its natural size: shared by
            # the main rooms up to half again their depth; anything beyond that
            # becomes a room of its own at the back (a sitting room downstairs,
            # an open terrace upstairs) or, if too small for one, goes to the
            # biggest room.
            if spare > 1e-3 and rs:
                takers = [r for r in rs if r.grow and r.cap - r.depth > 1e-3]
                for r in takers:
                    r.depth += min(spare * r.depth / sum(t.depth for t in takers), r.cap - r.depth)
                spare = (hi - lo) - sum(r.depth for r in rs)
                growable = [r for r in rs if r.grow]
                if 1e-3 < spare < 1.2 and growable:
                    max(growable, key=lambda r: r.depth).depth += spare
                    spare = 0.0
            if self.level > 0 and getattr(self, "below", None):
                self._flip_suites(rs, u0, u1, hi)
            cursor = hi
            lead = abs(hi - D) < 0.01          # rows from the front, for an L's reach
            for r in rs:
                b0 = cursor - r.depth
                if r.widths:
                    lead = False
                    hall_low = abs(u0 - self.spine[1]) < 0.01
                    a = u0 if hall_low else u1
                    for part, w in zip(r.parts, r.widths, strict=True):
                        if hall_low:
                            add(part.type, a, b0, a + w, cursor, part.req); a += w
                        else:
                            add(part.type, a - w, b0, a, cursor, part.req); a -= w
                elif len(r.parts) == 1:
                    wide = getattr(self, "reach", 0.0) if (lead and r.parts[0].type in (T.LIVING, T.DRAWING, T.VERANDAH)) else 0.0
                    if not wide:
                        lead = False
                    ua, ub = (u0 - wide, u1) if getattr(self, "reach_low", True) else (u0, u1 + wide)
                    add(r.parts[0].type, ua, b0, ub, cursor, r.parts[0].req)
                else:
                    tot = sum(max(p.area, 1.0) for p in r.parts)
                    a = u0
                    outer_low = abs(u0 - self.house[0]) < 0.01
                    parts = sorted(r.parts, key=lambda p: (p.type in WETS) != outer_low)
                    for p in parts:
                        w = width * max(p.area, 1.0) / tot
                        add(p.type, a, b0, a + w, cursor, p.req)
                        a += w
                cursor = b0
            if cursor - lo > 0.05:
                gap = cursor - lo
                if self.level > 0 and gap >= 1.5 and (abs(lo - self.v0) < 0.01 or g):
                    add(T.TERRACE, u0, lo, u1, cursor, name="Terrace")
                elif self.level == 0 and gap >= 2.5 and abs(lo - self.v0) < 0.01:
                    # Garden: the shorter wing stops short, and the house is an L.
                    # The floors above stop there too - nothing overhangs the garden.
                    self.garden[(round(u0, 2), round(u1, 2))] = cursor
                elif gap >= 1.4 and not (rs and rs[-1].grow):
                    add(T.STORE, u0, lo, u1, cursor, name="Store")
                elif rs:
                    # Too small to be a room: every room on the last row reaches down to close it.
                    for room in self.rooms_ref:
                        c = room.metadata.get("_c")
                        if c and abs(c[1] - cursor) < 0.01 and c[0] >= u0 - 0.01 and c[2] <= u1 + 0.01:
                            nc = (c[0], lo, c[2], c[3])
                            room.polygon = self._poly(*nc); room.metadata["_c"] = nc
        return True
